title_old: High-Protein Breakfast Meal Prep Ideas (Under $2 a Serving)

replacements.find: Below are breakfast meal-prep ideas that land under $2 a serving, hit real protein numbers
replacements.replace: Below are breakfast meal-prep ideas that cost a fraction of the drive-thru, hit real protein numbers

replacements.find: Eggs, at roughly $0.25 to $0.35 each right now, give you about 6 grams of protein apiece.
replacements.replace: Eggs run ~$0.14 each and give you about 6 grams of protein apiece.

replacements.find: Cottage cheese runs about $0.40 per half-cup serving and brings 12 to 14 grams.
replacements.replace: Cottage cheese runs ~$1.82 a pound, and a half-cup serving brings 12 to 14 grams.

replacements.find: And a big tub of plain Greek yogurt, around $5 for 32 ounces, breaks down to about $0.60 per serving with 17 grams of protein.
replacements.replace: And a big tub of plain Greek yogurt runs ~$2.24 a pound, with 17 grams of protein per serving.

replacements.find: Here is the math on a solid version. A dozen eggs at $3.50, a cup of shredded cheese at $1.00, a half-pound of diced ham at $2.00, and a handful of frozen veggies at $0.50 comes to $7.00 for 12 muffins. That is about $0.58 per muffin.
replacements.replace: Here is a solid version. A dozen eggs, a cup of shredded cheese, a half-pound of diced ham, and a handful of frozen veggies make 12 muffins.

replacements.find: Eat two for breakfast and you have a $1.16 meal delivering around 20 grams of protein. Add a piece of fruit and you are still under $2.
replacements.replace: Eat two for breakfast and you have a cheap meal delivering around 20 grams of protein. Add a piece of fruit and it still costs a fraction of that drive-thru sandwich.

replacements.find: Cost per jar looks like this. Rolled oats run about $0.20 a serving from a big canister, milk about $0.15, Greek yogurt about $0.60, and a spoon of peanut butter for another $0.20. That is roughly $1.15 a jar for about 22 grams of protein.
replacements.replace: Every piece of it is a cheap staple: rolled oats from a big canister, milk, Greek yogurt, and a spoon of peanut butter. Together they bring about 22 grams of protein a jar.
